newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria names Dutchman as new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria names Dutchman as new chief executive.

text.p: Shell Nigeria said on Monday a new chief executive had been appointed for the company, one of the most difficult jobs in the Anglo-Dutch group.

Incumbent Brian Anderson, a Briton born in Nigeria 54 years ago, told a news conference he had been appointed chairman of Shell companies in Greater China and would be succeeded in Nigeria by a Dutchman, Ron van den Berg, currently chief executive of Shell companies in Brunei.
The new man is expected to take up his position in July. Anderson has held the Nigeria job for three and a half years.
Shell came under world-wide criticism in the last one and half years over the November 1995 hanging of nine Ogoni minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa for murder.
Human rights and other pressure groups felt Shell did not use its influence in stopping Nigerian authorities from executing the nine after a trial widely considered flawed.
Anderson said Shell was "misunderstood and unjustly criticised" over the Ogoni issue.
The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria accounts for about 50 percent of the country's two million barrels per day (bpd) production of crude oil.
Shell has been under fierce international scrutiny since the company was forced to leave Ogoniland in the southeastern Niger Delta in 1993 amid sabotage and attacks on its staff.
Anderson restated Shell's position that the company had no plans to resume oil production in Ogoniland for now.

"We will not resume production in Ogoni until we have concluded talks with all factions of Ogoniland," he said, adding, "We are keen but we think we must reach common understanding with all the parties in the area."
